selection: taglib (4,118) is the only C++ library among the 25 Homebrew hits with a documented local byte/stream API that parses MPEG frame headers. Its MPEG::File over a ByteVectorStream reports version, layer, sample rate, channels, bitrate and duration for both untagged Layer III controls. Higher-ranked mpg123 (12,256) and lame (6,992) are C libraries and belong to the C cell; the C++ hits mp3val, mp3check, mp3blaster, ncmdump and mp3fs are programs without a documented library API.
family: TagLib MPEG frame-header and tag parser; the same TagLib 2.3.2 library as the active mp3_id3v2/cpp taglib entry. This is a separate plain-frame scope, not an independent parser family.
uncertainty: One verified path; no padding. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for six queries, captured 2026-11-17; header-only C++ decoders and vcpkg/Conan packages were not searched. Homebrew installs measure demand for the whole TagLib distribution, mostly as a tag library, not use of its MPEG property API. TagLib parses frame headers and does not decode audio; for CBR streams without Xing/VBRI its duration comes from stream size and the first frame's bitrate. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.
